name: 64-solenoid Shiva hat OBE case (Saroka 2010): 20->6 ms, pause, 100->30 ms
origin: Saroka, Mulligan, Murphy & Persinger 2010 (Persinger's lab), 64-coil Shiva headset
summary: The two 5-min exposures of a single case from Persinger's lab: the amygdala burst-firing signal stepped counter-clockwise through the 8 strips of a 64-solenoid hat, 20 ms on the left frontal strip and 2 ms less on each next, then 1.5 min without field, then 100 ms and 10 ms less on each next. A 27-year-old man reported floating seconds after the first exposure ended (Saroka 2010 p.9 [474]). One coil per strip here.
notes: Saroka 2010 reports one 27-year-old man in a hat of 64 solenoids 'in columns of 8 separated by 45 deg' (p.4 [469]). The 8 strips, each running from the apex to the side of the skull, were switched on in turn, from left frontal to right prefrontal: 5 min with 20 ms on the first strip and 2 ms less on each next, down to 6 ms, 1.5 min without field, then 5 min with 100 ms and 10 ms less on each next, down to 30 ms (p.5 [470]). The signal had 289 points of 3 ms, so 'one sequence of the pattern was completed every 867 msec' (p.5 [470]). The experience 'did not occur during the presentation of either field configuration. It began within seconds after the termination of the 20+2 configuration' (p.9 [474]). EEG: a power peak at 2 Hz over the left temporal lobe (p.6 [471]) and theta and low-beta coherence between left temporal and right frontal sites (p.7 [472]). This file plays the same sequence and timings on 8 single coils, one per strip. Each strip shrinks to one point, so the 'global' field over the upper head, to which the paper attributes the effect, is lost. The burst is this project's rising sweep (6 to 30 Hz) with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers. It repeats without a gap, because the paper mentions no silence between bursts. Field: 'approximately 1 uT', an 'estimated intracerebral strength' (pp.4, 9 [469, 474]); how it was measured is not stated. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. This is a single uncontrolled case. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The man had fatigue and a headache afterwards: have someone present, and stop at once on anxiety, nausea or headache. Not for people with epilepsy or prone to anxiety.
setting: The source session took place in a small office with normal low lighting (400 lux) and people walking in the hallway, with the man seated and EEG recorded (Saroka 2010 p.4 [469]). This project's safety advice, not the source setting: sit or lie in a quiet room with someone present who can stop the session.
schedule: Two 5-min exposures with 1.5 min without field between them, as in the paper (Saroka 2010 p.5 [470]). No repeat schedule was published. Keep at least a week between sessions, as Murphy advises for Shiva.
source: Saroka, Mulligan, Murphy & Persinger 2010, NeuroQuantology 8(4):466-477 (ResearchGate listing) https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275606923_Experimental_Elicitation_of_an_Out_of_Body_Experience_and_Concomitant_Cross-Hemispheric_Electroencephalographic_Coherence ; PRLog press release (2012) https://www.prlog.org/11844110-god-helmet-inventor-induces-out-of-body-experience-in-under-six-minutes-using-quiet-magnetic-fields.html ; Murphy blog: OBE in less than six minutes https://sacredneurology.com/2017/08/01/out-of-body-experience-in-under-six-minutes-with-advanced-magnetic-stimulation/ ; Murphy, Psychic Skills & Miracles lecture https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tmC1174POpA ; Ryczko & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 95:592 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434855/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
